prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation supplies distribution circuits through transformer/feeder bays. Automation covers bay control/monitoring, station coordination, external interfaces; primary equipment, protection and wiring follow approved designs/limits. Station observation remains separate from local control/protection.
Bay Automation Controller (Juniper) sequences bays, evaluates status/permissives, produces Bay Status Digest, requests breaker operations only under permitted modes/permissives. North Bay Controller and South Bay Controller automate respective portions.
Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem) detects faults and initiates protection within its configured zone; produces Relay Diagnostic Note for self-monitoring conditions requiring engineering attention. Trips must remain independent of routine control; control failures cannot inhibit clearing.
Breaker Control Unit executes authorized operations, enforcing electrical/mechanical interlocks. Local selection gives local authority precedence; remote commands require station authority, bay selection, interlocking, availability.
Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing) consolidates station/bay indications, operating conditions and communication quality; coordinates supervision, produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip. Displays do not replace local indications; supervision performs no dedicated protection. Commands require configured permissions/procedures; local interlocks/equipment logic remain authoritative. Visibility depends on communications/status quality; interruptions cause stale/unavailable displays; operators must confirm currency after recovery.
Station Gateway carries supervisory communications to authorized remote interfaces. Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin) acquires satellite reference, distributes time via configured network; produces Clock Drift Snapshot at configured offset-reporting condition. Timestamps aid correlation, not measurement/protection validity. Reference loss invokes device-specific, potentially degrading holdover; time-quality indications distinguish synchronized/degraded/unavailable timing.
Station DC System supplies automation/protection power within capacity; loss can interrupt supervision/time distribution until restoration. Sequence Event Archive retains events. Engineering Workstation supports authorized configuration/maintenance under controlled access. Maintenance Remote Terminal allows approved maintenance without replacing local authority.
Control Room Operator assesses displays, coordinates operation, verifies commanded states. Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur) maintains settings/evaluates performance under approved changes. Substation Field Crew follows switching instructions/clearances. Substation Supervisor oversees supervisory use/escalates unresolved availability concerns.

Document units:
S052: The Feeder Protection Relay provides local protection for its assigned feeder and operates independently of supervisory control availability.
S053: Its approved setting group defines the pickup levels, time delays, and logic required for the feeder protection scheme.
S054: The Protection Relay Engineer develops setting changes against the approved protection study and the current equipment data.
S055: The Protection Relay Engineer documents the engineering basis and expected operational effect for each proposed change.
S056: Engineering Workstation maintains the working configuration under revision control.
S057: Engineering Workstation produces the Settings Review Receipt after a settings review is completed.
S058: Each proposed change receives a unique revision identifier before review begins.
S059: The Protection Relay Engineer verifies that proposed values agree with the approved coordination objectives.
S060: A second qualified reviewer independently checks calculations, logic changes, and device applicability.
S061: The review confirms that the proposed configuration is complete, internally consistent, and suitable for the intended feeder.
S062: Coordination checks consider upstream and downstream protection behavior across the expected operating range.
S063: Protection settings are not approved solely on the basis of copied values from another installation.
S064: Engineering Workstation retains the approved configuration and its revision history for controlled access.
S065: Configuration access is limited to personnel with assigned engineering responsibilities.
S066: The Protection Relay Engineer records the approval status before any setting change is released for implementation.
S067: Before deployment, the approved configuration is checked against the intended device model and firmware version.
S068: A controlled outage or other approved work window is required when implementation could affect feeder protection.
S069: The Substation Field Crew follows the authorized work instructions during device access and setting transfer.
S070: After installation, the implemented values are compared with the approved configuration.
S071: The Feeder Protection Relay is functionally checked to confirm the intended protection behavior after a change.
S072: Any discrepancy stops release of the configuration until its cause is resolved and reviewed.
S073: The Substation Supervisor ensures that engineering changes follow the established authorization and operational control process.
S074: The Substation Field Crew is known operationally as Cinder during field activities.
S075: Cinder performs inspections, maintenance, and switching support within the boundaries of approved work.
S076: Field access begins only after the required work authorization and site entry controls are confirmed.
S077: The Control Room Operator coordinates operational access with the Switching Desk Coordinator before work that could affect energized equipment.
